summary: Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin, attested in 2009.

Jinshi Fan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University (~1958–1963). She served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy (~1998–2014) and held a post at Lanzhou University.

Jiro Sugiyama (1928–2011) was a Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952). He held posts at the Tokyo National Museum (~1952–1988), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1988–1993), ICPBS, and Bukkyo University.

Jitendra Nath Banerjea (1895–1966) was an Indologist and historian who studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918). He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1952–1959).

Jitendranath Mohanty (1928–2023) worked in philosophy and Indology, studying at the University of Calcutta (~1947–1949) and the University of Göttingen (~1952–1954). He held posts at Calcutta (~1954–1967), Oklahoma (~1972–1986), and Temple University (~1986–2008).
Jitsuaki Oshika (b. 1919) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and served as a professor at Toyo University, attested in 1980–1981.

Jiyu Ren (1916–2009) worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1934–1938), he served as director of the Institute of World Religions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, attested in 2000.

Joachim Gentz works in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He served as Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and as Reader in Chinese Studies at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2013).
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Vienna by 1994, studying under Gerhard Oberhammer.

Joachim Wach (1898–1955) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Leiden University. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1924–1935) and as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1945–1955).
Joan Halifax (b. 1942) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied at H. Sophie Newcomb Memorial College (~1960–1964) and the University of Miami (~1969–1973).

Joanna Gottfried Williams (1939–2022) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University (1960–1969), she served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1967 to 2022.

Joanne Punzo Waghorne specializes in religious studies and Indology. After studying at the University of Chicago (~1969–1976), she held posts at UMass Boston (1975–1983), Bowdoin College (1983–1985), UNC Chapel Hill (1987–2002), and Syracuse University (2002).

Joe Bransford Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and the University of Virginia (PhD 1984), later teaching at Virginia (1981–1985) and UNC Wilmington (attested 1994–2001).

Joe Cribb (b. 1947) works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of London (~1966–1970), he served as Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1970–2010).
Joey Hung (b. 1991) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Hong Kong Academy for Performing Arts and held a post at Dharma Drum Buddhist College around 2008.
Jogendra Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara under the instruction of Uma Shankar Vyas.

Jogindra Nath Samaddar (1884–1929) was an Indologist and historian educated at Presidency University and Bangabasi College. He taught at Pramatha-Manmatha College, St. Columba's College, and served at Patna College (1912) and Patna University (1923).

Johan Elverskog (b. 1968) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at Indiana University (~1995–2000) and has held a professorship at Southern Methodist University since ~2002.
Johann Andreas Schmeller (1785–1852) was a linguist who held positions at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1826–1852) and the Bavarian State Library (~1829–1852).
